column3: The Greek describes His sitting rather than explicitly the act of sitting down.
“Said” renders Greek present “says”; the Greek asks where they should buy, rather than explicitly where they can.
The Greek speaks of bread worth two hundred denarii being insufficient; BSB makes the money the subject of buying.
“What difference will these make” expands the Greek “what are these for so many?”
The Greek first names taking the loaves, then mentions fish separately after distributing; BSB combines loaves and fish at the start.
“Said” renders present “says”; the Greek leaves the filled persons unnamed rather than explicitly “everyone.”
The Greek explicitly names seizing Him before making Him king.
BSB converts twenty-five or thirty stadia to miles and renders present “see” as past.
“Jesus” supplies the unnamed subject; “spoke up” renders present “says.”
The Greek says the boats came; BSB specifies landing.
“These” is not separately stated before signs.
“Of approval” supplies an interpretation of the sealing image.
Both Greek questions use present verbs, rather than future “will perform” and “will do.”
